meaning:
συμβούλιον, -ου, τό
(σύμβουλος), [in LXX: 4Ma.17:17 א * ;]
a word of the Græco-Roman period (of. Lat. consilium, and see Deiss., BS, 238) = cl. συμβουλία (Arist., Xen.),
1. counsel: σ. λαμβάνειν, Mat.12:14 22:15 27:7 28:12; διδόναι, Mrk.3:6 (ποιεῖν, Rec.); ποιεῖν, Mrk.15:1 (ἑτοιμάζειν, WH, mg.).
2. By meton., a council (4Mac, l.with א; συνέδριον, AR): Act.25:12 (see MM, xxiv).†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: But the Pharisees went out, and conspired against him, how they might destroy him.
The Pharisees went out, and immediately conspired with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him.
Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, “You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you shall go.”
